faq.answer: There is no single facet count used by every Big Five instrument. This directory follows the thirty-facet NEO/IPIP-NEO vocabulary. BFI-2 uses fifteen facets. Identify the particular instrument and its definitions before comparing structures.
faq.question: Is thirty the official number of Big Five facets?

faq.answer: No. An educational page and a personal measurement are different things. Your questionnaire and report must explicitly identify a reported facet before you interpret its score. Five domain scores cannot be used to reconstruct thirty unreported facet scores.
faq.question: Does a facet page mean my test measured that trait?

faq.answer: Start with the situation you want to understand. For example, hesitation about joining a group may concern group preference, initiating contact, being evaluated, or practical constraints. Choose one or two plausible facets and check the alternatives. If the question is still broad, begin with the parent domain.
faq.question: Which facet should I read first?

faq.answer: A broad result does not determine every narrower tendency. First confirm that the report provides both levels, then check the instrument's scoring and score metric. Do not assume equal weighting or explain every difference as high and low facets cancelling out. Percentiles cannot simply be averaged.
faq.question: Why might a domain result and its facets seem inconsistent?

faq.answer: No. You may have had few relevant opportunities or overlooked contrary behavior. Separate genuine opportunities without the expected behavior from occasions when the behavior was not possible. Comparable natural observations can support a provisional everyday idea; limited patterns call for a narrower idea, and unclear evidence calls for setting it aside.
faq.question: If I find no counterexamples, have I confirmed the trait?

faq.answer: That pattern alone cannot establish a problem or its cause. Check whether the report actually contains facet scores, their direction and reference, the questionnaire version, and how the items were answered. Do not infer a diagnosis, a response bias, or a temporary negative self-view from the pattern alone.
faq.question: What if all thirty reported facets are low?

faq.answer: It shows what happened with that practice under those conditions. Record deliberate preparation or environmental changes separately from spontaneous behavior. A later test difference also requires attention to instrument, language, scoring, timing, and measurement error before it can be interpreted as trait change.
faq.question: Does a successful practice mean my personality changed?

faq.answer: Not automatically. NEO and IPIP-NEO concern similar constructs but use different instruments, and IPIP-NEO versions can select different items. BFI-2 has a different facet structure. Direct score comparison requires evidence about the measures, metrics, and reference samples, rather than a match between names.
faq.question: Can similarly named facets from different tests be compared?

faq.answer: They can suggest questions about a work setting, but they do not establish skill, performance, or fit. Someone who rarely takes the conversational lead may still have strong leadership skills. Career exploration also needs actual task information, interests, demonstrated abilities, resources, and experience.
faq.question: Can facets tell me which career I would perform well in?

faq.answer: No. They are facet names in this personality tradition. Temporary states, recurring tendencies, and clinical conditions should be distinguished. Persistent distress or difficulty functioning should be assessed by a qualified professional rather than diagnosed from a personality label.
faq.question: Are Anxiety, Depression, or Impulsiveness diagnoses?

not_for: Do not use this page for clinical diagnosis or as the sole basis for hiring or admission.
method_boundary.summary: Use this page to understand personality concepts and examine everyday behavior. Interpret actual scores using the instrument’s scoring method, reference sample, and intended use.

sections.body:
A broad description can feel accurate in one setting and unhelpful in another. You might enjoy welcoming someone into a small gathering while avoiding a crowded event. Those experiences raise separate questions about warmth and preference for groups; the word extraversion alone does not settle them.

A facet is a narrower tendency within a personality domain. A particular invitation, conversation, or decision is an event shaped by its circumstances. The event may offer a clue, but it cannot establish a facet or explain its own cause.

Start with something you want to understand: Which kinds of company do I seek? What makes it difficult to start a task? When do I reconsider a familiar view? Choose one or two relevant facets and keep the question specific enough to examine.

Higher, lower, and middle positions describe a continuum. They do not divide people into separate types or rank their worth. This page provides an interpretive vocabulary, not personal measurements. A facet's presence in the directory does not mean your questionnaire assessed it.
sections.heading: Use the directory to sharpen a question

sections.body:
FermatMind's public directory uses the NEO/IPIP-NEO interpretive vocabulary: six facets under each of five domains. This is one way of organizing narrower tendencies. It is not a universal list required by every Big Five instrument.

The [official IPIP guide](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm) describes a 300-item NEO-related inventory and two 120-item selections developed using different methods. The same item count therefore need not identify the same questionnaire. IPIP scales are intended to measure constructs similar to NEO facets; they are not the proprietary NEO instrument.

Names also differ. The [NEO/IPIP comparison table](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEO_FacetsTable.htm) pairs Warmth with Friendliness, Deliberation with Cautiousness, and other related labels. Such correspondence does not make the items, scores, or reference samples interchangeable. The [BFI-2 authors' description](https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/bfi.html) identifies a different inventory with 60 items and 15 facets.

Before interpreting a result, identify the instrument, version, language, reported scales, and score metric. If your report gives only five domains, this directory cannot supply the missing facet scores. It can help you decide what to ask next.
sections.heading: Thirty facets belong to a particular tradition

sections.body:
Read [Openness](/en/personality/big-five/openness) for orientation, then follow the question that matters:

- [Imagination](/en/personality/big-five/facets/imagination): inner scenes and imagined possibilities.
- [Aesthetics](/en/personality/big-five/facets/aesthetics): engagement with art and beauty.
- [Feelings](/en/personality/big-five/facets/feelings): vividness of emotional experience and attention to it.
- [Actions](/en/personality/big-five/facets/actions): willingness to try unfamiliar activities.
- [Ideas](/en/personality/big-five/facets/ideas): interest in abstract questions.
- [Values](/en/personality/big-five/facets/values): willingness to reconsider established views.

These distinctions prevent one interest from standing in for the whole domain. Someone may enjoy discussing an unfamiliar ethical argument while preferring a familiar daily routine. Ideas and Actions concern different experiences. Feelings does not measure emotional regulation skill, and interest in ideas does not establish intelligence.

If you avoid a new class, consider whether the obstacle is novelty, cost, scheduling, or lack of access. If you spontaneously explore unfamiliar material in another setting, keep that example too. The useful question is where the pattern appears, rather than which broad label fits one choice.
sections.heading: Openness: separate different kinds of experience

sections.body:
The [Conscientiousness](/en/personality/big-five/conscientiousness) facets direct attention to different parts of organizing and undertaking tasks:

- [Competence](/en/personality/big-five/facets/competence): confidence in handling tasks.
- [Order](/en/personality/big-five/facets/order): preference for organization.
- [Dutifulness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/dutifulness): the pull of commitments and obligations.
- [Achievement Striving](/en/personality/big-five/facets/achievement-striving): pursuit of demanding goals.
- [Self-Discipline](/en/personality/big-five/facets/self-discipline): starting and continuing tasks.
- [Deliberation](/en/personality/big-five/facets/deliberation): considering consequences before acting.

Competence here concerns a person's sense of effectiveness; actual skill needs separate evidence. Wanting an ambitious outcome does not guarantee a prompt start. Deliberation concerns consideration before action, while Self-Discipline concerns getting underway and following through.

Suppose a renewal form remains unfinished. You might be uncertain about a requirement, waiting for necessary documents, overwhelmed by other obligations, or putting off an available task. Record which conditions apply before treating the delay as a personality pattern. A prepared checklist that helps on the next occasion is evidence about that support, not a new trait score.
sections.heading: Conscientiousness: distinguish confidence, obligation, and follow-through

sections.body:
Begin with [Extraversion](/en/personality/big-five/extraversion), then distinguish:

- [Warmth](/en/personality/big-five/facets/warmth): friendly closeness with people.
- [Gregariousness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/gregariousness): attraction to group company.
- [Assertiveness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/assertiveness): taking initiative and expressing a position.
- [Activity](/en/personality/big-five/facets/activity): preferred pace and amount of activity.
- [Excitement Seeking](/en/personality/big-five/facets/excitement-seeking): attraction to intense stimulation.
- [Positive Emotions](/en/personality/big-five/facets/positive-emotions): experiences of joy and enthusiasm.

Being welcoming does not require wanting a large audience. A busy pace does not establish productivity. Assertiveness does not establish sound judgment or leadership skill, and Positive Emotions cannot tell you how quickly someone recovers from stress.

If you hesitate to host an event, ask what you are hesitating about: the size of the group, initiating contact, practical work, expense, or the expectation of entertaining everyone. Each calls for a different next step. One hesitation cannot determine your position on the domain.
sections.heading: Extraversion: company, initiative, pace, and enjoyment

sections.body:
Within [Agreeableness](/en/personality/big-five/agreeableness), the directory separates:

- [Trust](/en/personality/big-five/facets/trust): expectations about other people's intentions.
- [Straightforwardness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/straightforwardness): expression without deception or manipulation.
- [Altruism](/en/personality/big-five/facets/altruism): willingness to help.
- [Compliance](/en/personality/big-five/facets/compliance): yielding or reducing confrontation in conflict.
- [Modesty](/en/personality/big-five/facets/modesty): reluctance to emphasize personal importance.
- [Tender-Mindedness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/tender-mindedness): consideration of suffering and need.

Concern does not require agreement. Helping someone does not show that you trust every person, and being straightforward does not require revealing private information. Compliance describes a tendency in disagreement; it is not an instruction to accept an unreasonable demand.

For example, you might offer a friend a lift while declining to lend your car. The two decisions concern different requests and consequences. Neither provides a general verdict on kindness, trust, or character. Examine the choice and its conditions before assigning a label.
sections.heading: Agreeableness: helping and yielding are separate questions

sections.body:
Read [Neuroticism](/en/personality/big-five/neuroticism) alongside these narrower terms:

- [Anxiety](/en/personality/big-five/facets/anxiety): tension, worry, and fear.
- [Anger](/en/personality/big-five/facets/anger): irritation and anger.
- [Depression](/en/personality/big-five/facets/depression): low mood and negative self-feelings.
- [Self-Consciousness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/self-consciousness): discomfort about being noticed or evaluated.
- [Impulsiveness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/impulsiveness): difficulty resisting strong urges.
- [Vulnerability](/en/personality/big-five/facets/vulnerability): feeling unable to cope under pressure.

Self-Consciousness is not a general measure of self-reflection. Impulsiveness in this tradition concerns urges and restraint, rather than every quick decision. Vulnerability is not a verdict that a person is weak or lacks practical coping skills.

These are facet labels, not diagnoses. A difficult afternoon, a recurring tendency, and a clinical condition require different kinds of understanding. Neither a directory nor a personality score can establish a diagnosis. Persistent distress or interference with daily life warrants assessment by a qualified professional; you do not need to settle on a facet label first.
sections.heading: Neuroticism: identify the experience without making a diagnosis

sections.body:
A broad domain cannot specify every narrower tendency. Two people with similar Agreeableness results could differ in their willingness to help, their initial trust, and their approach to disagreement. One might volunteer readily while carefully checking unfamiliar requests; another might readily assume good intentions but protect their time by declining help. These are conceptual examples, not inferred facet scores.

If an instrument reports both levels, consult its actual scoring rules. Do not assume that six facets are equally weighted, that a domain must be their simple average, or that facet percentiles can be combined into a domain percentile. A difference between reported scores does not explain itself.

The same care applies to combinations. Several higher and lower results do not create a new personality type. A middle result does not automatically mean flexibility or balance. Select the distinctions relevant to your question, then examine behavior and circumstances. A numerical gap between facets cannot establish why someone acted as they did.
sections.heading: Similar domain results can leave different questions unanswered

sections.body:
Consider the question: Why do I welcome time with a friend but hesitate when several people suggest a shared outing? Start with [Warmth](/en/personality/big-five/facets/warmth) and [Gregariousness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/gregariousness). Avoid translating either choice into a global introvert label.

Make the working idea precise: When I am free, interested in the activity, and comfortable with the people involved, I tend to choose meeting one person over joining a larger group. The target behavior is choosing the individual meeting when both options are genuinely available and comparable. Check that either can be chosen freely, that the activities and company are similarly appealing, and that time, transport, cost, noise, fatigue, or caring responsibilities do not make one option impractical. Record what you chose and why. Enjoying the conversation and skillfully managing it are separate observations.

**Opportunity without the expected behavior:** An individual meeting and a larger gathering both meet those conditions, but you freely choose the gathering. The target behavior—choosing the individual meeting—did not occur. Record the reason and any remaining differences between the options. This is one exception to record; it does not by itself overturn a usual preference or prove a Gregariousness level. Declining a group invitation alone cannot show which option you prefer.

**No relevant opportunity:** Only the group invitation is available, or work or transport prevents you from choosing one of the two options. There is no usable comparison. Record that limitation rather than treating attendance or nonattendance as evidence of the preference or as a counterexample.

**A natural exception:** Keep an unprompted choice of the gathering over a genuinely comparable individual meeting as a natural observation. One such choice can coexist with a tendency to choose individual meetings. Check what made it different. If choices vary mainly with the activity, narrow the idea to that activity, such as a preference for individual meetings when the purpose is quiet conversation. If group choices recur under comparable conditions, reconsider how often the original pattern occurs and whether the explanation still fits.

**A planned attempt:** For one manageable occasion, agree on an end time and choose a quieter venue. Record that these conditions were intentionally arranged, whether you attended, and whether the arrangement made the experience workable. This examines a practical support. It does not establish your usual unassisted preference or prove that your personality changed.

Keep an idea provisionally when natural observations repeatedly fit comparable conditions and no clear opposing pattern has emerged. Narrow it when the pattern belongs to particular settings. Set it aside when opportunities are scarce, circumstances are unclear, or competing explanations remain unresolved. Not finding a counterexample is not the same as showing that none exists. These notes can improve everyday choices; they are not a personality validation exercise.
sections.heading: A practical example: wanting connection without wanting every group

sections.body:
For the broad model, return to the [Big Five overview](/en/personality/big-five). For a specific experience, follow the relevant facet link above. If several names seem interchangeable, read their parent domain and compare the two definitions closest to your question before adding more labels.

If you have a report, check which facets it actually provides and what the numbers mean. A percentile needs an identified reference population; a number displayed out of 100 does not explain its own metric. If the report has no facet results, use the directory to organize questions rather than manufacture measurements.

The [official IPIP construct guide](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm), [NEO/IPIP comparison table](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEO_FacetsTable.htm), [long-form item material](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEOFacetsKey.htm), [Maples short-form item material](https://ipip.ori.org/30FacetNEO-PI-RItems_Maples_etal.htm), and [BFI-2 authors' page](https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/bfi.html) explain terminology and instrument differences. Statistics in those materials belong to the instruments and studies described there. They do not establish the reliability, validity, or norms of a FermatMind assessment.

The examples here are prompts for checking everyday explanations. They are not questionnaire items, clinical interventions, or promises of trait change. For career exploration, also examine the work itself, interests, demonstrated skills, resources, and direct experience. A tendency alone cannot establish occupational fit or individual performance.
